title: Allow zellij run CLI command to block until command has completed
body:
The `zellij run` command should have the ability to block until the command being run has exited.

This would allow zellij to be invoked in scripts or shortcuts to perform actions and then have control returned to the caller.

For example, my use case is using Helix keybinds to invoke the Yazi file browser to select a file to which will then be opened in Helix. However currently I am unable to block until I've selected a file as the zellij command immediately exits.

comments.body:
I have this working with Yazi and Helix specifically:

```toml
# config.toml
[keys.normal."'"]
y = ":sh zellij run --floating -n 'yazi picker' -- /home/<user>/.config/fish/scripts/open_in_helix_from_yazi.fish"
```

```fish
# open_in_helix_from_yazi.fish
set -l tmpfile /tmp/yazi-choice.txt
rm -f $tmpfile
yazi --chooser-file=$tmpfile
zellij action toggle-floating-panes
zellij action write 27 # send escape-key
zellij action write-chars ":<nick> $(cat /tmp/yazi-choice.txt)"
zellij action write 13 # send enter-key
zellij action toggle-floating-panes
zellij action close-pane
```

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
In the meantime, one workaround to achieve blocking calls to `zellij run` would be to use [FIFO](https://<redacted-host>/linux/anonymous-named-pipes)s (aka named pipes). It's a bit hacky but still simple enough. Here's an example with fish:

```fish
set id (uuidgen)
mkfifo /tmp/$id
zellij run -fc -- fish -c "fzf | tee /tmp/$id"
cat < /tmp/$id > /dev/null
rm -rf /tmp/$id
```

This will run `fzf` and block until the command is done executing.

Or, even shorter with process signals:

```fish
zellij run -fc -- fish -c "fzf; kill -s CONT $fish_pid"
kill -s STOP $fish_pid
```

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
Thanks for suggesting this feature.

A few things:
1. This is possible with plugins using the new [pipe interface](https://zellij.dev/documentation/plugin-pipes). The flow would be "pipe to a plugin from the CLI which will be launched if not running, the plugin could either do whatever it wants on its own or launch a command passed to it, then unblock the CLI once the command is done".
2. Zellij also has in a built-in [filepicker](https://zellij.dev/tutorials/filepicker/) that does exactly this. Maybe it's not as nice as the dedicated Yazi, but it can at least serve as an example of how this can be achieved.

While I totally empathize with people wanting this to be part of core, the philosophy of this project is to offload as much as possible to plugins in order to help us maintainers keep up. If someone makes a generic plugin that blocks until a command is done, I'd be happy to link to it and refer to it when this comes up.

ADDENDUM: if someone is interested in implementing this plugin and wants support, they are welcome to join our Discord - there are lots of plugin authors there who'd be happy to help.

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
The bash script assumes that the escape key puts the mode back to normal.
In my case, the escape key is mapped to capslock and within Helix, my escape key toggles between NORMAL and INSERT mode. So consider making it explicit by mapping the keys in the Helix config like this:

```toml
# ~/.config/helix/config.toml
[keys.normal]
C-y = [
  "normal_mode",
  ":sh zellij run -f -- bash ~/picker.sh"
]
```

and do not write the escape key in the sh script.

comments.author: participant11
comments.body:
For anyone interested in an example of opening yazi in a **side-pane** (not a floating pane) from a helix keybind & persisting it in view, I'm posting here just because this took me a bit of digging to figure out but it turned out quite nice actually.

(referencing the note in [yazi-docs](https://github.com/yazi-rs/yazi-rs.github.io/blob/0f0f5206797757ae5e4688a201ca2bb195e173fa/docs/tips.md#file-tree-picker-in-helix-with-zellij-helix-with-zellij)):

> Note: this uses a floating window, but you should also be able to open a new pane to the side, or in place. Review the Zellij documentation for more info.
---
config.toml
```
[keys.normal]
C-y = ":sh zellij run -d right -- bash ~/.config/helix/yazi-picker.sh"
```

Edit: something changed where the while/do stopped working. I've updated my script:
```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
zellij action move-pane left

while true; do
	paths=$(yazi --chooser-file=/dev/stdout | sed 's/^/"/;s/$/"/' | tr '\n' ' ')

	if [[ -n "$paths" ]]; then
		zellij action focus-next-pane
		zellij action write 27 # send <Escape> key
		zellij action write-chars ":<nick> $paths"
		zellij action write 13 # send <Enter> key
		zellij action focus-previous-pane
	fi
done
```

Edit2: I've been modifying & improving my script (i.e open where you left off, fixed memory leak issue with yazi processes not closing). I'm just gonna link the most up-to-date version I have on my github dot-file repo here for ya: https://github.com/participant11/dot-configs/blob/main/helix/yazi-picker.sh

comments.author: participant12
comments.body:
> For anyone interested in an example of opening yazi in a **side-pane** (not a floating pane) from a helix keybind & persisting it in view, I'm posting here just because this took me a bit of digging to figure out but it turned out quite nice actually.
>

@participant11 that helped a lot! 

Not sure if there's an easier way with yazi, but I needed to make this small change to have it remember the directory it was in after opening a file.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e

PREV_DIR="/tmp/yazi_location.${ZELLIJ_SESSION_NAME}.${ZELLIJ_PANE_ID}"
touch $PREV_DIR

zellij action move-pane left

while true; do
    if [ -s "$PREV_DIR" ]; then
      paths=$(yazi $(cat $PREV_DIR)  --chooser-file=/dev/stdout | while read -r; do printf "%q " "$REPLY"; done)
    else
      paths=$(yazi --chooser-file=/dev/stdout | while read -r; do printf "%q " "$REPLY"; done)
    fi

    eval "PATHS=($paths)"
    if [[ -n ${PATHS[@]} ]]; then
      FIRST=${PATHS[-1]}
    fi

    if [[ -e $FIRST ]]; then
      echo $(dirname $FIRST) > $PREV_DIR
    fi

    if [[ -n "$paths" ]]; then
        zellij action focus-next-pane
        zellij action write 27 # send <Escape> key
        zellij action write-chars ":<nick> $paths"
        zellij action write 13 # send <Enter> key
        zellij action focus-previous-pane
    fi
done
```
